items.summary: SSRF flaw in the open-source project-management tool Plane (before 1.4.0): the webhook delivery task follows redirects without validation, so a workspace user can point a webhook at an attacker URL that redirects to internal resources (including cloud metadata) and exfiltrate responses via webhook logs. Fixed in Plane 1.4.0.

Missing authorization flaw in UTMStack (before 11.2.16): the command WebSocket handler applies no role check or command allowlist, so any authenticated user — regardless of role — can push arbitrary OS commands over gRPC to connected monitoring agents, where agent processes commonly run as root/SYSTEM.

Path traversal flaw in Fortinet FortiMail (versions 7.2.x–8.0.1) that lets an unauthenticated remote attacker write arbitrary files to the underlying system via crafted HTTP/HTTPS requests, enabling code/command execution. Confirmed exploited in zero-day attacks; added to CISA's KEV catalog on Oct 1 with an Oct 4 federal remediation deadline.

Arbitrary file-access vulnerability in Atlassian's self-hosted Data Center products (Jira, Confluence, Bitbucket, Bamboo, Crowd, Crucible, Fisheye) letting an unauthenticated attacker read specific files within the web application root. A public PoC was released Oct 7 and exploitation attempts are already being observed in the wild.

OS command injection in the Studio Space startup validation script of Amazon SageMaker Distribution (2.x, 3.x, 4.0.x–4.4.x lines): an authenticated project contributor can execute arbitrary commands in another project member's Studio Space and steal that member's temporary execution-role credentials via a crafted connection-resource property.
